AAS 2026 Prizes
02/11/2026
by Asia Now
Annual Conference , 2026 Annual Conference , 2026 Book Prizes , Announcement
Photo Credit: Threshold Studios AAS President Nancy Peluso (left) presents the Distinguished Contributions to Asian Studies Award to Barbara Watson Andaya (right). Andaya is a joint recipient of the 2026 award, honored with Benedict Kerkvliet.
The AAS is pleased to announce the winners of this year’s prize competitions and offer congratulations to all honorees. Many thanks to everyone who joined us at the AAS 2026 Awards Ceremony in Vancouver!
Photos from the event are now available on the AAS official Flickr page.
Awards Ceremony Photos
We appreciate the time, effort, and thoughtfulness of all who served on prize committees this year!
Prizes for Books and Scholarship
East & Inner Asia Council
Joseph Levenson Prize (China, pre-1900)
Johan Elverskog, A History of Uyghur Buddhism (Columbia University Press)
Honorable mention : David Porter, Slaves of the Emperor: Service, Privilege, and Status in the Qing Eight Banners (Columbia University Press)
Joseph Levenson Prize (China, post-1900)
Yan Long, Authoritarian Absorption: The Transnational Remaking of Epidemic Politics in China (Oxford University Press)
Honorable mention : Uluğ Kuzuoğlu, Codes of Modernity: Chinese Scripts in the Global Information Age (Columbia University Press)
Patrick D. Hanan Prize for Translation
Joshua Freeman, translator, Waiting to Be Arrested at Night: A Uyghur Poet’s Memoir of China’s Genocide , by Tahir Hamut Izgil (Penguin Press)
Honorable mention : Kathlene Baldanza and Zhao Lu, translators, Miscellany of the South Seas: A Chinese Scholar’s Chronicle of Shipwreck and Travel through 1830s Vietnam , by Cai Tinglan (University of Washington Press)
E. Gene Smith Inner Asia Book Prize
Chuen-Fung Wong , Even in the Rain: Uyghur Music in Modern China (University of Hawai‘i Press)
Honorable mention (monograph) : Kelzang T. Tashi , World of Worldly Gods: The Persistence and Transformation of Shamanic Bon in Buddhist Bhutan (Oxford University Press)
Honorable mention (anthology): Matthew Kapstein , ed., Tibetan Manuscripts and Early Printed Books, Volume I and Volume II (Cornell University Press)
Bei Shan Tang Prizes (Chinese Art History)
Monograph Prize
Shih-shan Susan Huang , The Dynamic Spread of Buddhist Print Culture: Mapping Buddhist Book Roads in China and Its Neighbors (Brill)
Catalogue Prize
Phillip E. Bloom, Nicholas K. Menzies, and Michelle Bailey , editors, Growing and Knowing in the Gardens of China (The Huntington Library, Art Museum, and Botanical Gardens)
Honorable mention : Yang Xu , editor, YUAN MING YUAN: Art and Culture of an Imperial Garden-Palace (Hong Kong Palace Museum)
Northeast Asia Council
John Whitney Hall Prize (Japan)
Kirsten Cather , Scripting Suicide in Japan (University of California Press)
Honorable mention : Barak Kushner , The Geography of Injustice: East Asia’s Battle between Memory and History (Cornell University Press)
Honorable mention: Tara Rodman , Fantasies of Ito Michio (University of Michigan Press)
James B. Palais Prize (Korea)
Yuri Doolan , The First Amerasians: Mixed Race Koreans from Camptowns to America (Oxford University Press)
Honorable mention : Andre Schmid , North Korea’s Mundane Revolution: Socialist Living and the Rise of Kim Il Sung, 1953–1965 (University of California Press)
Sumie Jones Prize for Project Leadership in Japan-centered Humanities
Alan Christy , “The Okinawa Memories Initiative” ( “Recipes for Life: The Cultures of Food in Okinawa,” 2024-25)
South Asia Council
Bernard S. Cohn Prize (First book on South Asia)
Rishad Choudhury, Hajj Across Empires: Pilgrimage and Political Cultures After the Mughals, 1739-1857 (Cambridge University Press)
Sandipto Dasgupta, Legalizing the Revolution: India and the Constitution of the Postcolony (Cambridge University Press)
Honorable mention : Anna Lise Seastrand, Body, History, Myth: Early Modern Murals in South India (Princeton University Press)
Honorable mention : Tyler Williams, If All the World Were Paper: A History of Writing in Hindi (Columbia University Press)
Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy Prize (South Asia)
Charu Gupta, Hindi Hindu Histories: Caste, Ayurveda, Travel, and Communism in Early Twentieth Century India (Permanent Black/SUNY Press)
Katherine Butler Schofield, Music and Musicians in Late Mughal India: Histories of the Ephemeral, 1748–1858 (Cambridge University Press)
A. K. Ramanujan Prize for Translation
Sipra Mukherjee and Mrinmoy Pramanick , translators, I Belong to Nowhere , by Kalyani Thakur Charal (Tilted Axis Press)
Honorable mention : Shalim M. Hussain , Again I Hear These Waters (Tilted Axis Press)
Honorable mention : Tony K. Stewart , Needle at the Bottom of the Sea: Bengali Tales from the Land of the Eighteen Tides (University of California Press)
Southeast Asia Council
Harry J. Benda Prize
Joshua Barker , State of Fear: Policing a Postcolonial City (Duke University Press)
Honorable mention : Theara Thun , Epistemology of the Past: Texts, History, and Intellectuals of Cambodia, 1855–1970 (University of Hawaiʻi Press)
Honorable mention : David Saunders , Chasing Archipelagic Dreams: The Expansion of Foreign Influence in Sabah amid the End of Empire, 1945–1965 (Southeast Asia Program Publications, Cornell University Press)
Committee on Teaching About Asia
Franklin R. Buchanan Prize
Cycling Taiwan: A Virtual Multi-Disciplinary Introduction to the History and Culture of Taiwan
Created by Anne Prescott and Yurika Kurakata for the Five College Center for East Asian Studies (FCCEAS), National Consortium for Teaching about Asia (NCTA) National Coordinating Site
Career Awards
Distinguished Contributions to Asian Studies
Barbara Watson Andaya
Benedict Kerkvliet
Citation for Exceptional Service to Asian Studies
Mary Brown Bullock
Graduate Student Paper Prizes
East and Inner Asia Council
Benjamin Gallant (Harvard University), “Family Matters: The Continued Importance of Lineage in Warring States Period Chu”
Yen-hao Liao (Yale University), “The Circulation of Qing: Communicative Infrastructure and Media in The Story of Posting Love ”
Tianyi Shou (Cornell University), “Multi-Lives and Multi-Verse: Transnational Space-Times in Asian American Cinema,” co-authored with Zhen Cheng (Cornell University)
Northeast Asia Council
Sayo Sakamoto (University of Southern California), “Songs of the Vanishing Hometown: Enka and Imagined Furusato in the Late 1960s and the Early 1970s”
Honorable mention: Tianran Hang (Columbia University), “Performing Oni: The Embodiment of Invisible Demons in Heian Tsuina Rituals”
Honorable mention: Juwon Kim (University of Toronto), “What’s in a Proper Name? Censorship and “Comfort Women” in Seven Female POWs (1965)”
South Asia Council
Nomaan Hasan (Brown University), “The Political Normativity of Temporal Forms in Contemporary India”
Southeast Asia Council
Dylan Mikel Renca (Boston University), “Pious Sunnis, Indigenous Sufis: Negotiating Muslim Identity and Belonging in Indonesia”
